idea-plugin.name: Hotspots Veyra
idea-plugin.description:
A living heat map of your codebase. Find the files where bugs live.

Some files cause most of the trouble: they're complicated and they change all the time. Hotspots Veyra reads your project's own git history, finds those files, and shows your whole codebase as one heat map, with who knows each file, which files secretly change together, and the code only one person understands.

What you get

  • The hotspot map: every file is a tile, sized by its code and coloured by risk. Hover for details, click a file for its full story, double-click to open it, click a folder's name to zoom in.
  • Five ways to look: Hotspots, Change frequency, Complexity, Code age and Knowledge risk.
  • Top Hotspots, ranked: the files to refactor first, with the reason spelled out.
  • Changes Together: pairs of files that keep landing in the same commits, often across folders. A hidden dependency, made visible.
  • Knowledge Risks: files only one person has changed, and code whose only author has left.
  • 🔥 in the Project view on the hottest files, and the open file's rank in the status bar.
  • Why Is This a Hotspot?, File History with each commit's diff, and a Markdown report for your team.

How it's measured

Change frequency comes from your git history (the last year by default). Complexity comes from the file's lines of code and how deeply they're indented, which follows nesting in every language: Java, Kotlin, Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, C#, PHP and the rest. The hotspot score is the two multiplied, each on a log scale.

Private

Everything happens on your computer: Hotspots runs git log and reads your files, and that's all. No account, no telemetry.

Open it from View → Tool Windows → Hotspots. Works in every JetBrains IDE: IntelliJ IDEA, Android Studio, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, PhpStorm, Rider, CLion, RubyMine and RustRover.
Made by FlightCoders, the team behind Veyra Studio.
